title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Edits that no longer eat your code
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.9 fixes edits that destroyed code. Organize Imports could replace a class body, Remove unused function could delete everything up to the file header, Rename rewrote imports of unrelated symbols, and a quick fix that was supposed to add a release() call had never appeared at all.

highlights.title: Organize Imports keeps the class body
highlights.description: An import inside a raw string or a KDoc sample used to mark the end of the import block, and everything between the real imports and that line was replaced. The block is bounded to the file header now, for Organize Imports, Add import and the unused-import check alike.

highlights.title: Remove unused function stays on the function
highlights.description: A /* px */ at the end of the line above made the removal climb to the nearest /* in the file. Rename also touches only the import of the renamed symbol, and follows $name into string templates.

highlights.title: A quick fix that finally shows up
highlights.description: "Add release() in onStop()" looked up its pairing table by the wrong name and never appeared; it does now, inside the class, with the enclosing function's indentation. The outline reads the live document while it is dirty.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Offers no cross-file "Remove unused parameter" edit when the owner's name is declared elsewhere too, and computes edits on open editors' unsaved text.
Resolves "Add names to call arguments" through the file's imports instead of the first homonym indexed.
